lessons.title: Describing nouns with verbs
lessons.explanation: Use ~는 것 to turn a verb phrase into a noun-like expression, such as ‘the act of studying’ or ‘the thing that I like’. This lesson is the foundation for the next several lessons.

cards.translation: The thing I want most is a car
cards.explanation: Use the present modifier to describe the noun by what someone wants.

cards.translation: I want my friend to bring apples
cards.explanation: Use the present modifier before 것 for an action in progress or viewed generally.
cards.source_sentence: 저는 친구가 사과를 가져오는 것을 원해요

cards.translation: My dream is becoming a teacher
cards.explanation: Use the modifier form before a noun-like expression.

cards.translation: I like watching movies
cards.explanation: Use the present modifier when the action is treated as a thing.

cards.translation: The food I ate
cards.explanation: Use the past modifier when the action happened before the noun reference.

lessons.meaning: Turns a verb clause into a noun-like expression with 것, often meaning the thing or action that someone does, wants or likes.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when an action needs to be discussed as a thing or when a noun is described by what somebody does.
lessons.how_to_build: Use a verb in the present modifier form ~는 before 것. Add the past or future modifier forms before 것 when the time reference requires them.
examples: 내가 가장 원하는 것은 차야
The thing that I want most is a car
저는 친구가 사과를 가져오는 것을 원해요
I want my friend to bring apples
나의 꿈은 선생님이 되는 것이다
My dream is becoming a teacher
저는 영화를 보는 것을 좋아해요
I like watching movies
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Using ~던/었던 to Describe Past Tense
lessons.explanation: Use ~던 for a remembered repeated or continuing past action and ~았/었던 for a remembered action or state that has finished. The neutral ~ㄴ/은 form is a comparison, not the target of this lesson.

cards.translation: That is the computer I had used last year
cards.explanation: Use the remembered-past form that matches whether the event was ongoing/repeated or completed.

cards.translation: I threw out all the tissue paper that the baby had used
cards.explanation: Use the remembered-past form that matches whether the event was ongoing/repeated or completed.
cards.source_sentence: 저는 애기가 썼던 휴지를 다 버렸어요

cards.translation: I again studied for the exam that I once gave up on
cards.explanation: Use the remembered-past form that matches whether the event was ongoing/repeated or completed.

cards.translation: The president gave money to those who once lived here
cards.explanation: Use the remembered-past form that matches whether the event was ongoing/repeated or completed.
cards.source_sentence: 대통령이 여기에 살았던 시민들에게 돈을 줬어요

cards.prompt: 우리가 지난 주에 ___ 내용을 다시 공부할 거예요
cards.translation: I will study the contents that we had learned last week again
cards.explanation: Use the remembered-past form that matches whether the event was ongoing/repeated or completed.
cards.source_sentence: 우리가 지난 주에 배웠던 내용을 다시 공부할 거예요

lessons.source_title: Lesson 27: Using ~던/었던 to Describe Past Tense
lessons.meaning: ~던 and ~았/었던 describe a noun from the speaker's remembered experience. ~던 commonly presents a repeated past action that continued up to the relevant time; ~았/었던 presents a past action or state as finished and no longer continuing. The ordinary past modifier ~ㄴ/은 is the neutral comparison form.
lessons.when_to_use: Use ~던 when you recall something that happened repeatedly or was continuing. Use ~았/었던 when you recall something that happened before but has ended or is no longer true. The difference is a nuance of memory and completion, so the context matters.
lessons.how_to_build: Put the verb or adjective before the noun (or 것). For verbs, attach ~던 to the stem for the remembered/repeated or continuing sense: 입다 → 입던. For a finished remembered event or state, insert the past form before 던: 입다 → 입었던, 예쁘다 → 예뻤던. Do not use the neutral ~ㄴ/은 examples as target answers for this lesson.
examples: 이 빵은 슬기가 자주 먹던 빵이야
This is the bread Seulgi used to eat often
이곳에 근무하던 우체국 직원이 삶을 영원히 포기했어요
The post-office employee who used to work here gave up on life forever
우리가 지난 번에 먹었던 곳에서 먹고 싶어요
I want to eat at the place where we ate last time
작년에 사업에 실패했던 남자가 새로운 기술을 발견했어요
The man who failed at his business last year discovered a new technology
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: More uses of ~는 것
lessons.explanation: Build on ~는 것 with irregular verbs, preference expressions, and common noun-like constructions. Pay attention to how the form combines with 이다 and particles.

cards.translation: Who is the person that built that house?
cards.explanation: Apply the irregular present modifier before the noun.

cards.translation: I will build a house
cards.explanation: Use the future modifier for an intended or expected action.

cards.prompt: 그 사람은 서울에서 부산까지 ___ 첫 번째 사람이었다
cards.translation: That person was the first person who walked from Seoul to Busan
cards.explanation: Use the irregular modifier that fits the completed action.
cards.source_sentence: 그 사람은 서울에서 부산까지 걸은 첫 번째 사람이었다

cards.translation: Is there something I can help you with?
cards.explanation: Use the future/possible modifier before the noun-like 게.

cards.translation: I saw my friend open the door
cards.explanation: Use the noun-like expression for an action that was observed.
cards.source_sentence: 저는 친구가 문을 여는 것을 봤어요

lessons.meaning: The lesson develops further uses of ~는 것, including irregular forms, preferences and situations where an action is treated as a noun.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when Korean needs to say what somebody likes, wants, finds difficult or is referring to as an action or thing.
lessons.how_to_build: Build the noun expression with the correct present modifier before 것; apply the irregular stem changes and particles shown in the lesson.
examples: 그 집을 지은 사람은 누구예요?
Who is the person that built that house?
저는 집을 지을 거예요
I will build a house
그 사람은 서울에서 부산까지 걸은 첫 번째 사람이었다
That person was the first person who walked from Seoul to Busan
제가 도울 게 있나요?
Is there something I can help you with?

lessons.title: Nominalizing with ~기 and ~ㅁ/음
lessons.explanation: Use ~기 and ~ㅁ/음 to turn verbs and adjectives into nouns. These forms overlap with ~는 것 but have different common patterns and registers.

cards.prompt: 쌀을 물에 넣은 후에 쌀의 색깔이 ___ 시작했어요
cards.translation: After I put the rice in the water, the color of the rice started to change
cards.explanation: Nominalize the verb or adjective in the form that fits the following predicate and register.
cards.source_sentence: 쌀을 물에 넣은 후에 쌀의 색깔이 변하기 시작했어요

cards.translation: I don’t want to eat
cards.explanation: Nominalize the verb or adjective in the form that fits the following predicate and register.

cards.translation: I don’t want to wash the rice
cards.explanation: Nominalize the verb or adjective in the form that fits the following predicate and register.

cards.translation: I will go for a run
cards.explanation: Nominalize the verb or adjective in the form that fits the following predicate and register.

cards.translation: I’m bad at skipping
cards.explanation: Nominalize the verb or adjective in the form that fits the following predicate and register.

lessons.meaning: ~기 and ~ㅁ/음 nominalize verbs and adjectives. HTSK compares these noun forms with the earlier ~는 것 construction.
lessons.when_to_use: Use ~기 for many everyday noun expressions and ~ㅁ/음 for written, formal or statement-like noun forms where the lesson uses it.
lessons.how_to_build: Attach ~기 to the stem, or form the appropriate ~ㅁ/음 ending from the stem; then add particles or following predicates.
examples: 나의 여자 친구는 내가 사과를 가져오기를 원해
My girlfriend wants me to bring apples
나는 밥을 벌써 먹기 시작했어
I already started eating rice
나는 밥을 먹기 싫어
I do not want to eat rice
나는 네가 먹고 있음을 알았어
I knew that you were eating

lessons.title: Expressing uncertainty and duration
lessons.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

cards.translation: I don’t know where my friend is going
cards.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

cards.translation: I don’t know where my friend is going
cards.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

cards.translation: I don’t know who mom is eating with
cards.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

cards.translation: I don’t know what mom is eating
cards.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

cards.translation: I don’t know where mom is eating
cards.explanation: Use ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지, and ~(으)ㄹ지 to express uncertainty. You will also see these forms used with 얼마나 and for actions continuing over a period of time.

lessons.meaning: ~는지, ~(으)ㄴ지 and ~(으)ㄹ지 express uncertainty or an indirect question. ~지 can also combine with time expressions to say how long it has been.
lessons.when_to_use: Use them when the speaker does not know whether something is true, asks an embedded question, or measures time since an event.
lessons.how_to_build: Match the ending to a present action, adjective or noun, past event, or future possibility, then place the clause before 알다, 모르다 or a similar predicate.
examples: 수술을 받을지 안 받을지 확실하지 않아요
It is not certain if I will get surgery or not
그가 제 말을 들었는지 안 들었는지 모르겠어요
I don’t know if he was listening to me or not
저는 엄마가 밥을 먹었는지 안 먹었는지 모르겠어요
I don’t know if mom ate or not
제가 구한 아르바이트가 좋은지 안 좋은지 모르겠어요
I don’t know if the job I found is good or not

lessons.title: ~는 것 with 이다
lessons.explanation: Apply the ~는 것 principle to 이다 and use the contraction ~는 거예요 in natural spoken Korean.

cards.translation: Seulgi is doing something illegal
cards.explanation: Apply the ~는 것 principle to 이다 and use the contraction ~는 거예요 in natural spoken Korean.

cards.translation: Leonardo Dicaprio, who is an actor in Titanic is handsome
cards.explanation: Apply the ~는 것 principle to 이다 and use the contraction ~는 거예요 in natural spoken Korean.

cards.translation: I don’t know if that person is a teacher or not
cards.explanation: Apply the ~는 것 principle to 이다 and use the contraction ~는 거예요 in natural spoken Korean.

cards.translation: I didn’t know that we were the same age
cards.explanation: Apply the ~는 것 principle to 이다 and use the contraction ~는 거예요 in natural spoken Korean.

cards.translation: I don’t know where the emergency exit is
cards.explanation: Apply the ~는 것 principle to 이다 and use the contraction ~는 거예요 in natural spoken Korean.

lessons.meaning: ~는 것이다 and the spoken ~는 거예요 identify, explain or emphasize what something is. The lesson applies 것 with 이다.
lessons.when_to_use: Use it when clarifying the nature of an action, correcting an interpretation, or presenting the important point of a sentence.
lessons.how_to_build: Make the noun-like clause with 것 and attach 이다; use the appropriate tense and polite contraction such as 거예요 in speech.
examples: [직업이] 선생님인 사람들은 인기가 많아요
People whose job is teaching are popular
내 친구는 부자인 아버지를 자랑했어
My friend showed off his rich father
그 사람이 선생님인지 모르겠어요
I don't know whether that person is a teacher
lessons.source_note: The guide is a concise paraphrase of the official HTSK lesson; the examples are separate sentences taken from that lesson page, not from the SRS cards.

lessons.title: Purpose and trying
lessons.explanation: Use ~려고 and ~러 to express purpose, and ~아/어 보다 to say that you try or experience doing something.

cards.translation: I am going to the event to see the performance
cards.explanation: Use ~(으)러 with a movement verb to express purpose.

cards.translation: I tried to eat rice
cards.explanation: Use ~려고 to state the purpose or intention of the action.

cards.translation: I tried eating rice
cards.explanation: Use ~아/어 보다 for trying an action or having the experience.

cards.translation: I try to meet that friend every weekend
cards.explanation: Use ~려고 before a verb of effort or intention.
cards.source_sentence: 그 친구를 매 주말 만나려고 노력해요

cards.translation: I am trying to learn Korean
cards.explanation: Use ~려고 to show the goal of the effort.

lessons.meaning: ~려고 and ~러 express purpose, while ~아/어 보다 means to try an action or to have the experience of doing it.
lessons.when_to_use: Use the purpose forms when one action is done in order to do another; use 보다 when talking about trying or experiencing an action.
lessons.how_to_build: Use verb stem + ~려고, or verb stem + ~(으)러 with a movement verb. Attach ~아/어 보다 to the verb stem and conjugate 보다.
examples: 공연을 보러 행사에 가고 있어요
I am going to the event to see the performance
공연을 보러 행사에 갈 거예요
I will go to the event to see the performance
나는 밥을 먹으려고 노력했다
I tried to eat rice
나는 밥을 먹어 봤다
I tried to eat (the) rice

lessons.title: The noun 중
lessons.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

cards.translation: I am eating
cards.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

cards.translation: I am studying
cards.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

cards.translation: I am studying
cards.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

cards.translation: I am thinking
cards.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

cards.translation: That building is under construction
cards.explanation: Learn two common uses of 중: after a verb with ~는 것 to mean ‘in the middle of doing’, and after a group of nouns to mean ‘among’.

lessons.meaning: 중 means middle or among. The lesson uses ~는 중 for an action in progress and ~중에서 for choosing from a group.
lessons.when_to_use: Use 중 when something is currently underway or when comparing or selecting one item among several.
lessons.how_to_build: Use verb + ~는 중이다 for an action in progress; use noun + 중에서 for among/from a set, then add the normal predicate.
examples: 아저씨가 프린터를 복구하는 중이에요
The man is in the middle of repairing the printer
모든 프린터 중에 이것이 제일 싸요
Of all the printers, this one is the cheapest
나의 친구들 중에 나는 슬기를 가장 좋아해
Among my friends, I like Seulgi the most
밥과 빵 중에 밥이 더 맛있어요
Between rice and bread, rice tastes better
